# 100.00 USD parked in a USD account, having reached a CAD bank.
#
# The mirror of the shape Q-039 reports, and the one where the parked figure is
# *not* an artefact. `Assets:Suspense USD` is USD, the invoice is USD and the
# receivable is USD, so the split states the settlement outright — 100.00 USD,
# with its CAD value beside it because the entry is quoted in the bank's
# currency. Nothing has to be read off the bank and nothing has to be inferred.
#
# It is the bank that is foreign here, not `Assets:Suspense USD`. Naming only the
# transaction settles it correctly — the receivable and the split agree on USD,
# so no conversion arises — and naming the split has to reach the same place.
#
# What this fixture produces: a CAD transaction, `Assets:Bank` +139.00 CAD
# against `Assets:Suspense USD` −100.00 USD valued −139.00 CAD, neither split
# in a lot.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
2026-03-04 * "Money in, USD parked, CAD bank"
	guid: "11223344556677889900aabbccddeeff"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:Bank 139.00 CAD
		guid: "223344556677889900aabbccddeeff11"
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:Suspense USD -100.00 USD
		guid: "3344556677889900aabbccddeeff1122"
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "1.39"
		value: "-139.00"
